extract:
Phil Collins was born on 30 January 1951 in Chiswick, west London, and grew up in nearby Hounslow. A child actor who attended the Barbara Speake Stage School, he played the Artful Dodger in a West End production of Oliver! and appeared as an extra in the Beatles film A Hard Day's Night. His professional music career has spanned from the late 1960s, when he drummed with the band Flaming Youth, to farewell tours in the 2020s. He joined Genesis as drummer in 1970, replacing John Mayhew, and became the band's lead vocalist after Peter Gabriel departed in 1975.

Collins' formative influences ranged from jazz and big band drummers such as Buddy Rich to the Motown and Stax soul records he loved as a teenager. Alongside Genesis he played fusion with Brand X, and he did session work, including drumming on Brian Eno's records. The collapse of his first marriage in the late 1970s supplied the raw material for his solo debut. Face Value (1981), released on Virgin in the UK and Atlantic in the US and co-produced with Hugh Padgham, opened with In the Air Tonight. Its brooding drum-machine build and explosive gated-reverb drum entrance, a sound Collins and Padgham had developed on Peter Gabriel's third album, became one of the decade's signature sonic gestures. The album also featured the Phenix Horns from Earth, Wind & Fire.

Hello, I Must Be Going! (1982) continued the formula and scored a major hit with a cover of the Supremes' You Can't Hurry Love. No Jacket Required (1985) marked his commercial peak, with the brighter, horn-driven pop of Sussudio and One More Night and the duet Take Me Home. Around the same time he scored hits with Against All Odds (Take a Look at Me Now) and the Philip Bailey duet Easy Lover. ...But Seriously (1989) leaned toward social commentary with Another Day in Paradise, a song about homelessness that won the Grammy for Record of the Year. Serious Hits...Live! (1990) documented the accompanying tour. Both Sides (1993) was a stark, largely self-played and self-produced record. Dance into the Light (1996), released after he left Genesis, adopted lighter, world-music-tinged arrangements.

Collins' collaborations were extensive. He produced and played on Frida's Something's Going On and Eric Clapton's Behind the Sun. He drummed on Robert Plant's early solo albums and performed at both Live Aid venues on the same day in 1985, flying across the Atlantic on Concorde. He also sang on Band Aid's Do They Know It's Christmas? His later soundtrack work for Disney's Tarzan earned an Academy Award for You'll Be in My Heart.

Critically, Collins was often dismissed as the face of slick, ubiquitous 1980s soft rock, and his overexposure provoked a backlash in the 1990s. Later reassessment credited his drumming, his production innovations and his songwriting craft. Hip-hop and R&B artists sampled and covered his work, and the In the Air Tonight drum fill became a pop-culture touchstone. He is among the few artists to have sold over 100 million records both as a solo act and with a band. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Genesis in 2010.

Spinal and nerve injuries eventually left Collins unable to drum. He published his memoir Not Dead Yet in 2016, launched a comeback tour of the same name with his son Nicholas on drums, and the albums were reissued as 2016 remasters and deluxe editions. Genesis' The Last Domino? tour concluded in 2022, which Collins has indicated marked the end of his performing career.
title: Phil Collins
